1.title: 1. What a magician can do
1.content: Spellcasting . | Spells fall into five categories: Combat, Detection, Health, Illusion, Manipulation. (SR3 p.191–198) | You learn each spell at a specific Force. You can cast it at that Force or lower, never higher. (SR3 p.178) At character creation no spell can be bought above Force 6. (SR3 p.60) | Casting is a Complex Action: roll Sorcery plus up to as many Spell Pool dice as Sorcery dice. The TN is the target’s Willpower (mana spells) or Body (physical spells), or its Object Resistance. (SR3 p.107, p.182) | Drain: Power = Force ÷ 2 (round down) + the spell’s modifier, at the Damage Level shown. Resist with Willpower plus any number of Spell Pool dice, and reduce one level per 2 successes. (SR3 p.162, p.44) . | It’s Stun if the Force is no higher than your Magic, and Physical if it is higher, or if you’re astrally projecting. (SR3 p.162) | Every spell you’re sustaining adds +2 to Drain Power. (SR3 p.162) | . | Spell Pool = (INT + WIL + MAG) ÷ 3. (SR3 p.44) | . For the full step-by-step, including resistance, Spell Defense and Drain, see Spellcasting, Resistance & Drain. Conjuring . Hermetic mages call elementals: Earth, Air, Fire and Water. (SR3 p.186) . | You need a conjuring library and a hermetic circle, each rated at least the Force of the elemental, plus ritual materials costing about 1,000¥ × Force. (SR3 p.186; MitS p.169) | The elemental needs something to form from: a bonfire, a pool of water, and so on. (SR3 p.186) | An elemental can give five services: Aid Sorcery, Aid Study, Spell Sustaining, Physical Service, Remote Service. For Aid Sorcery, fire elementals help combat spells, air detection, water illusion and earth manipulation. No elemental helps health spells. (SR3 p.187) | . Shamans summon nature spirits, and only inside the spirit’s domain. (SR3 p.184, p.186) . | Summoning is an Exclusive Complex Action. The Conjuring Test is against TN = the spirit’s Force, and each success is one service. With no successes, nothing comes, but Drain still applies. (SR3 p.186) | Nature spirits vanish at sunrise and sunset, and any unused services are lost. (SR3 p.186) | A service is one use of one of the spirit’s powers, or a physical task such as attacking. (SR3 p.186) | The four families are (SR3 p.266–267): . | Spirits of Man: city, field, hearth | Spirits of the Land: desert, forest, mountain, prairie | Spirits of the Sky: mist, storm, wind | Spirits of the Waters: lake, river, sea, swamp | . | . Conjuring Drain: Power = the spirit’s Force, with the level set by comparing Force to your Charisma. Resist with Charisma. (SR3 p.162, p.187) . Ritual sorcery (MitS p.34–36) . | A team of magicians can cast one spell together. It builds over hours, but it can reach a target out of sight. | The team can have at most as many members as the lowest Sorcery rating among them. Everyone must know the spell at the chosen Force, and all must share a tradition (shamans of different totems may mix). | You need a hermetic circle or shamanic lodge rated at least the spell’s Force, plus ritual materials, which are used up whatever happens. | To reach a distant target you need a material link: a piece of the target, such as blood, hair or tissue. | Elemental manipulation spells can’t be cast as ritual sorcery. | . Foci (SR3 p.189–191; MitS p.169) . Foci are bonded with Karma. The core types are spell foci (one specific spell or a whole category), spirit foci, power foci, sustaining foci and weapon foci. Active foci are visible and vulnerable on the astral. A weapon focus lets you use an armed skill in astral combat.

11.title: Action economy  (SR3 p.104–108)
11.content: In your Combat Phase you take either two Simple Actions or one Complex Action. (SR3 p.104) . Separately, you may take one Free Action during any character’s Combat Phase, including your own. You can’t take one before your first Combat Phase of the first Initiative Pass. Free Actions taken in someone else’s phase resolve last in that phase. (SR3 p.105) A Free Action can also be taken in place of a Simple Action. (SR3 p.105) . Free Actions (SR3 p.105) . Activate cyberware · call a shot · change a smartgun’s fire mode · deactivate a focus · delay an action · drop an object · drop prone · drop a sustained spell · eject a smartgun clip · gesture · observe (no Perception Test) · speak a word or short phrase · allocate Spell Defense dice. Simple Actions (SR3 p.105–107) . | Action | Notes | . | Fire Weapon | One shot in single-shot, semi-auto or burst-fire mode. A single-shot weapon fires only once per Combat Phase. 12.title: Ranged combat  (SR3 p.109–114)
12.content: Attack Test ─▶ Dodge Test (optional) ─▶ Damage Resistance Test ─▶ Compare & stage . | Base target number from range: Short 4, Medium 5, Long 6, Extreme 9, using the band for your weapon on the Weapon Range Table. (SR3 p.111) Apply the modifiers below. | Attack Test: the ranged combat skill plus any Combat Pool dice. Count successes. No successes means a miss. (SR3 p.113) | Dodge Test (defender’s choice): Combat Pool dice only, against TN 4, plus 1 per 3 rounds of a burst or full-auto attack, plus 1 per meter of shotgun spread, plus the defender’s wound modifier. | Beat the attacker’s successes and the attack misses completely. A tie does not count. | Otherwise the dodge successes aren’t wasted. They add to your Damage Resistance successes. (SR3 p.113) | . | Damage Resistance Test: Body (including dermal armor) plus any Combat Pool dice left, against TN = weapon Power − armor, minimum 2. (SR3 p.113) | Determine the outcome: compare the attacker’s successes with the defender’s total (dodge + resistance). (SR3 p.113) . | Attacker ahead: stage the Damage Level up one step (L → M → S → D) per 2 successes over the defender’s total. | Defender ahead: stage it down one step per 2 successes over the attacker’s. Below Light, no damage. | Tie: base damage. | In ranged combat, staging stops at Deadly. Extra successes are discarded. (SR3 p.113) | . | . Worked example, from the rulebook (SR3 p.113) . Liam (Pistols 6) fires an Ares Predator (9M) and gets 5 successes. Snot (Body 5, ballistic armor 4, already Lightly wounded) dodges with all 5 Combat Pool dice against TN 5 (4, +1 for his wound) and gets 2. That’s not enough to dodge, but the 2 count. His Damage Resistance Test is 5 Body dice against TN 5 (9 − 4) and gets 1. Snot’s total is 3, Liam’s is . | Liam is 2 ahead, so the damage stages up once to 9S. | .

(SR3 p.122) | Defender: the same, also against base TN 4, modified. (SR3 p.122) | Most successes hits. A tie goes to the attacker. 24.title: Selling harvested chrome
24.content: Man & Machine has no separate resale rule for used implants, so sell them the same way as any other loot. Use the fencing rules (SR3 p.237–238): a 30% base, 5% per net success on the Negotiation, never below 10% or above 50%. Stolen chrome isn’t standard gear, so expect the Finding a Fence TN to rise. Example. A dead samurai’s smartlink (2,500¥) and retractable spur (11,500¥) (SR3 p.302) list at 14,000¥ together. The fence’s base offer is 4,200¥. Depending on the Negotiation, the deal can’t go below 1,400¥ or above 7,000¥. Optional flavor, not from the books. Tracking tags or corporate lockouts on stolen high-end implants, and a time limit for pulling chrome from a corpse, are good complications. If you use them, set the tests yourself; neither book gives numbers.

25.title: Being scanned  (SR3 p.237)
25.content: Cyberware scanners are usually rated 3–9. The scanner rolls its rating against TN 3 for typical cyberware and TN 6 for alphaware. More successes identify the implants more precisely.

52.title: Step 0: The wound  (SR3 p.125–126)
52.content: Physical and Stun each have 10 boxes. The Light / Moderate / Serious / Deadly thresholds are 1 / 3 / 6 / 10 boxes, and they add +1 / +2 / +3 to target numbers and −1 / −2 / −3 to Initiative. At 10 boxes you’re unconscious. | Stun past 10 boxes spills into the Physical track, and you’re knocked out. | Physical past 10 boxes: you can survive overflow up to your Body rating. Until someone stabilizes you, you take another box every (Body) Combat Turns. Past Body in overflow, you’re dead. | . See Actions & Combat for the full table.

53.title: Step 1: Stabilize a dying character  (SR3 p.129)
53.content: Only for a Deadly wound. First aid can stabilize a Deadly wound but can’t reduce it. | Medic rolls Biotech against TN 10, with the modifiers from the First Aid Table in step 2. One success stabilizes the patient: the extra box every (Body) Combat Turns stops. | If that fails, the patient rolls natural Body against TN 10. With a success they stabilize on their own. If that fails too, they die once the damage exceeds their Body rating. | Trauma patch (optional, last resort): the patient gets an extra Body Test to stabilize, against TN 4 + the rating of any dermal armor or blood filters. Success stops the overflow damage. It makes permanent damage more likely: +2 to the step 4 test. | When professional help arrives, such as a hospital or a DocWagon paramedic with better Biotech, it makes another Biotech Test and Body Test. | .

59.title: Stun damage  (SR3 p.126)
59.content: Stun runs on its own track and recovers much faster. No medicine or known spell helps; you just rest. | The patient rolls Body or Willpower, whichever is higher, against TN 2, plus current Stun and Physical injury modifiers. | Recovering one box takes 60 minutes ÷ successes. Erase the box, then roll again for the next one. | The patient must be resting completely. If they’re interrupted, they start over, and the new roll can’t beat the first one. | . 60.title: Worked example
60.content: Snot takes a Serious Physical wound (6 boxes) from a Predator. | Stabilize: not needed; it isn’t Deadly. | First aid, within the hour. Teammate Doc has Biotech 4 and a medkit, and it’s a city street (+1). The TN is 8 + 1 = 9, less 1 for Snot’s Body 5 = 8. Doc gets 1 success: the wound drops to Moderate (3 boxes). Treatment takes 15 ÷ 1 = 15 Combat Turns. | Magic. The team mage casts Treat, still within the hour, against 10 − Snot’s Essence 6 = TN 4, and gets 2 successes. Two boxes heal, leaving 1 box: Light. Drain is resisted at Moderate, Snot’s wound level when the spell was cast. Nobody can use first aid or healing magic on this wound again. | Aftermath: not needed; it wasn’t Deadly. | Need a doctor? Snot rolls Body 5 against TN 2 for a Light wound and succeeds. He’ll heal on his own. | Heal over time. Body 5 against TN 4 gets 2 successes: 24 hours ÷ 2 = 12 hours, above the 2-hour minimum. He needs at least a Low lifestyle for that time. | .

63.title: The house-rule framework
63.content: The specialist pages use this structure. It came from the original gists. The numbers are not from any SR3 book, and are much higher than the Companion’s baselines. For example, a “professional” bodyguard at 1,500¥ a night compares with the book’s 200¥ a day. They fit a high-paying campaign. Scale them to your table. Fee = base day rate × threat multiplier, plus hazard pay (a percentage of that), plus expenses. | Base day rate is set by the specialist’s tier in their main skill (1–3, 4–5, 6–7, 8+). | Threat multiplier, from about ×1 for routine work to ×3–×6 for heavy opposition. | Hazard pay for being on-site rather than working remotely, usually +50% to +100%. | Expenses and deposits: ammunition, reagents, fake IDs, drone and deck repairs. By the book, Johnson covers expenses only if they’re negotiated (MJLBB p.20–21). | . Fixers take a finder’s fee, which the books don’t quantify. The original gists suggested 10–30% depending on how rare the specialist is. Many top-tier freelancers will ask instead for an equal share of the team’s payout. That fits the Companion’s guidance that the fee is per runner (SRComp p.99).

104.title: Life with a SIN  (SR3 p.238–239)
104.content: You need a SIN to get a legal job, open a bank account, own property, go to school, rent an apartment, set up utilities, and travel legally, which includes buying a bus ticket. Your credstick carries your ID, licenses and permits, and can hold your fingerprints, palmprints and retinal prints. The cost is a data trail. Every legal purchase leaves credit records and inventory, and possibly video footage, and stores that realize they sold to shadowrunners will hand those records to the police. (SR3 p.273) .

123.title: Step 5: Spell Effect  (SR3 p.183, p.191)
123.content: Compare the caster’s remaining successes with the target’s resistance successes. | Target ties or wins: no effect. A tie goes to the target. | Caster wins: the net successes (caster − target) measure the effect. The spell’s description says what they buy. | No resistance roll (an object, or a willing subject): all the caster’s successes count, and 1 success always gives some effect. | Damaging spells: the chosen Damage Level stages up one level per 2 net successes, up to Deadly. | . 126.title: Worked example: Manabolt
126.content: Kestrel has Magic 6, Sorcery 5, and a Spell Pool of 4 (Intelligence 5, Willpower 5, Magic 6 → 16 ÷ 3 = 5, and she spent 1 earlier this turn). She casts Manabolt at Force 5, choosing Serious, at a guard with Willpower 4. She isn’t sustaining anything. | Preparation. Force 5, Serious, 5 Sorcery dice plus 3 Spell Pool dice. That leaves 1 pool die for Drain. | Targeting. She can see him and they’re both on the physical plane. | Sorcery Test. 8 dice against TN 4 (his Willpower). She gets 4 successes. | Resistance. The guard rolls Willpower 4 against TN 5 (the Force) and gets 1. Nobody is running Spell Defense for him. | Effect. 4 − 1 = 3 net successes. Two of them stage Serious up to Deadly; the third is left over. Combat spells ignore armor, so the guard takes a Deadly Physical wound. | Drain. Manabolt’s Drain is (Damage Level). Power is 5 ÷ 2 = 2, and the level is Serious, the level she chose, not the staged one. She rolls Willpower 5 plus her last Spell Pool die, 6 dice against TN 2, and gets 3 successes. Two of them take Serious down to Moderate. Force 5 isn’t higher than her Magic 6, so it’s Moderate Stun. | . If she had cast at Force 7 (assuming she’d learned it that high): Drain Power would be 3, and the Drain would be Physical, because 7 is higher than her Magic. If a mage were protecting the guard with Spell Defense and rolled 2 successes against TN 5, Kestrel’s 4 would drop to 2. The guard’s 1 resistance success would leave 1 net success: not enough to stage up, so he’d take Serious.
